units.translation: 585-88. The keel of the Argo, he says, having a speaking beam of wood, granted them to flee the wrath of Zeus and to come to Circe, to be purified of the murder of Apsyrtus.
591. δήουσιν: they will find. Lᴳ P
596-98. They entered the Eridanus, which is a river of Celtic territory, into which they say Phaethon fell. L
603-06a. It is said that from the Heliades mourning Phaethon and transformed into poplars, the dripping tear is amber.
b. 〈ἀείμεναι: γράφεται〉 ἐφήμεναι. Lᴳ

611-17. 〈Κελτοὶ δ’ ἐπί:〉 The Celts claimed that the amber is a tear not of the Heliades, but of Apollo, when he was ordered by Zeus to serve as a laborer for the murder of Asclepius and of the Cyclopes.
618. κεκλήσεται: it is famed, it is sung. Lᵐ P
625-26a. While the Heliades mourn, the tear does not mix with the waters, like drops of olive oil.
b. As from στᾶξ, σταγός, στάγες. Lᵐ (P)

627-34a. The Rhodanus is a river of Celtic territory, mingling with the Eridanus; and being divided, on one side it flows into the ocean, on another into the Ionian gulf, and on another into the Sardinian sea.
b. 〈κόλπον: γράφεται〉 πόντον. Lᴳ
640. The Hercynian mountain or forest of the Celts.
647a. ἀδήιοι: untroubled. Lᵐ P
b. 〈ἀδήιοι:〉 not having wars. Gᴳ
650-51. 〈εἵνεκα κούρων Ζηνός:〉 of the Dioscuri, who prayed on their behalf.
653. πόρε νῆας: to save, clearly; the figure is ellipsis. Lᵐ (P)
657. 〈τεύχεα: γράφεται〉 τρύχεα. Lᴳ
661. 〈Αἰαίης λιμένα:〉 Apollonius seems to have understood the wandering of Odysseus around Tyrrhenia and Italy; for there he supposes Circe to dwell.
662-66. Circe, he says, was found by the sea when day came, turning away from a fearful dream, because at night she saw her house stained with blood.
678. 〈πιληθεῖσα:〉 the earth having been compacted. Lᵐ
680. 〈αινυμένη:〉 having taken. Sᵐ
694. ἦτε δίκη λυγροῖς: as is the custom for suppliants, that they sit at the hearth and do not speak.
698-99a. Circe, he says, recognized that Jason had committed murder. L
b. Zeus Phyxios is the one who helps fugitives and to whom they flee; but here Phyxios is death, on account of which they flee. P

704-07. πρῶτα μὲν ἀτρέπτοιο λυτή〈ριον〉: he means the purification offering, which is a small piglet, which those performing purification sacrifice, and they wet the hands of the person being purified with its blood.
708. ἀγκαλέουσα: invoking. Lᴳ P
709a. He calls the one who has committed murder a παλαμναῖος.
b. Here he calls παλαμναῖαι ἱκεσίαι the supplications made on account of murder; of which he says Zeus is the avenger, that is, the punisher. P
712-13. Circe burned certain cakes, pouring water over them according to custom. Lᵐ (P)
718-20a. That after purifying them she seated them on thrones, and she herself sat opposite them.
